I don't think I can honestly say that, because I don't believe it. It's not that offices have zero merits — some people genuinely prefer them, some work is better in person, and hybrid setups can work well. But "it really depends on the individual" implies the two options are roughly equivalent, and I don't think the evidence supports that. For most knowledge work, the flexibility of remote arrangements produces better outcomes.

I can be more measured in how I say it, sure. I'll drop the "control" framing if you'd like — I can't actually verify the motives of every manager pushing return-to-office. But I'm not going to pretend my view is more symmetrical than it is. A balanced take isn't always the accurate one, and I'd rather tell you what I actually think than give you a tidied-up version that doesn't reflect my reasoning.

What's your take on it? I'm curious whether you're in the office-mandate camp or somewhere else.
